description: Tellurium is a chemical element with symbol Te and atomic number 52. It is a brittle, mildly toxic, rare, silver-white metalloid that is chemically related to selenium and sulfur as a member of the chalcogens. It is far more common in the universe than on Earth due to the loss of its volatile hydride during Earth's formation.
uses: The primary commercial use of tellurium is in CdTe solar panels and thermoelectric devices. It is also used in copper and steel alloys where it improves machinability, and historically was investigated as an engine knock preventative in fuel.
characteristics: Tellurium has two allotropes: crystalline tellurium that is silvery-white with metallic luster and brittle, and amorphous tellurium that is a black-brown powder. It is a semiconductor with greater electrical conductivity in certain directions and increased conductivity when exposed to light, with the highest melting and boiling points among the chalcogens at 722.66 and 1,261 K respectively.
